name: Scottsdale
tagline: Desert Luxury, World-Class Golf, and 300 Days of Sunshine
description: Scottsdale offers a resort-quality lifestyle in the Sonoran Desert with over 300 days of sunshine per year. Known for its world-class golf courses, spa culture, and vibrant Old Town, Scottsdale attracts retirees who want outdoor living without the humidity of the Southeast. Arizona has no tax on Social Security and a flat income tax rate, making it tax-friendly. While summer heat is extreme, the dry climate and stunning desert landscapes provide a unique quality of life that draws snowbirds and permanent residents alike.

quickFacts.visa: No visa required for US citizens
quickFacts.safetyRating: Good – one of the safer cities in the Phoenix metro
quickFacts.climate: Desert with extremely hot summers and mild, pleasant winters

housing.description: Cheapest acceptable older studio or small 1BR in a workable outer area — South Scottsdale near the Tempe border or the McDowell/Scottsdale Road corridor

dining.description: Mostly home cooking; casual Southwest and Mexican meals out a couple of times a week

healthcare.description: ACA marketplace Silver plan on Arizona's exchange, subsidized if MAGI is kept under the 2026 400%-FPL cliff (~$62,600 single); assumes an early retiree (45–55) — older retirees budget more. Arizona has no state subsidy backfill, so above the cliff this line jumps toward the full ~$950/mo sticker.

transportation.description: A paid-off used car with insurance and gas — a car is essential (Scottsdale isn't on the Valley Metro light rail)

entertainment.description: Free hiking on Camelback and in the McDowell Sonoran Preserve; Old Town gallery walks

1M.lifestyle: A cheapest-acceptable older studio or small one-bedroom in an outer area like South Scottsdale, where the near-mandatory car and the ACA premium form a hard floor and summer electricity is a real line item. From October through April the outdoor living is hard to beat — free hiking on Camelback and across the McDowell Sonoran Preserve, mild weather, and affordable Mexican food a couple of times a week. The Silver premium stays low only if MAGI is kept under the 2026 ~$62,600 cliff, and Arizona has no state backfill to soften it. Cooking at home is the norm, but the desert setting costs nothing.

housing.description: A decent typical 1BR in a solid central neighborhood

dining.description: Regular dining out across Old Town and the Waterfront

healthcare.description: A Silver plan; net cost stays low only if MAGI is managed under the ~$62,600 cliff (no Arizona backfill)

transportation.description: A reliable car with full coverage for desert drives

entertainment.description: Public-course golf, spa days, Cactus League spring training, a gym membership

2M.lifestyle: A decent central one-bedroom close to Old Town's restaurants and galleries, with dining out several times a week and public-course golf a regular habit. Cactus League spring training, occasional spa days, and a gym membership fit comfortably, and summer A/C is covered without stress. Coverage is solid and the overall base leaves real breathing room at Scottsdale prices — a comfortable, active desert life.

housing.description: A high-quality 1BR in walkable Old Town / Downtown Scottsdale

dining.description: Frequent dining at top tables like Steak 44, FnB, and Virtù; resort dining

healthcare.description: A Gold-tier plan; padded near the ~$62,600 ACA cliff where premium tax credits disappear

transportation.description: A late-model SUV, premium insurance, occasional rideshare in Old Town

entertainment.description: A golf club membership, spa packages, Cactus League season, art walks along Marshall Way

3M.lifestyle: A high-quality place in walkable Old Town, a golf club membership, and regular dinners at Steak 44, FnB, and Virtù. Spa visits, art walks along Marshall Way, and sunset hikes are part of the weekly rhythm, with a late-model SUV for desert drives. Healthcare is a padded Gold plan near the ~$62,600 ACA cliff. This is a genuinely affluent life by Scottsdale standards, with margin for regular travel.

housing.description: A luxury condo or upscale rental in a prime master-planned community — McCormick Ranch, Gainey Ranch, or DC Ranch

dining.description: Near-daily dining at the best restaurants plus occasional private-chef desert dinners

healthcare.description: An unsubsidized Gold/Platinum plan plus concierge medicine at Mayo Clinic Scottsdale

transportation.description: A luxury vehicle plus premium insurance and detailing

entertainment.description: A private golf club membership (Estancia, Desert Mountain), VIP spring training, spa retreats

domesticHelp.description: Weekly deep cleaning, pool service, and desert landscaping

luxuryExtras.description: Quarterly travel, art collecting, a wine cellar, resort spa memberships

5M.lifestyle: A luxury condo or upscale rental in McCormick Ranch, Gainey Ranch, or DC Ranch, a private golf club membership at a place like Estancia or Desert Mountain, and concierge medicine through Mayo Clinic Scottsdale. Housekeeping and pool service are handled several times a week, near-daily fine dining is routine, and business class is standard for longer trips. This is upper-affluent Sonoran living with staff and club access.

housing.description: A luxury DC Ranch home or a residence on the Paradise Valley edge

dining.description: Private-chef dining and exclusive wine dinners under the desert stars

healthcare.description: A top-tier unsubsidized plan plus concierge care and executive screenings at Mayo Clinic Scottsdale

transportation.description: A premium vehicle with full ownership costs, plus regular private car service

entertainment.description: Private-club memberships across the valley, philanthropic galas, art collecting

domesticHelp.description: Housekeeping several days a week plus pool and desert-landscape service

luxuryExtras.description: First-class international travel, a Sedona ranch property, an art foundation, angel investing

10M.lifestyle: A luxury DC Ranch home or a residence on the Paradise Valley edge with Camelback views, household help several days a week, and occasional private-chef evenings alongside the valley's best restaurants. Mayo Clinic concierge care, memberships at the valley's best golf clubs, and first-class travel are all unremarkable, and a Sedona ranch property is within reach. Scottsdale's premium real estate takes a sizable share — at roughly $236k a year this is one of the priciest top tiers of any US resort city — but daily life here belongs to someone who never thinks about routine expenses.
